Recently there have been a LOT of posts about reddit, and that was to be expected. A lot of Voat users are ex or (as in the case of myself) current redditors, some leaving because of "toxic" communities, others looking for a different kind of community, and a few just curious. These posts vary from news (a little too much news if you ask me) to opinion pieces.

But this is a post about Voat. I come here because there are less people, and less people usually means a more friendly community. Yet the abject hatred being directed at reddit in almost every single post is shocking. The comments here are just as toxic, if not more, than those on the other site. They are vicious and aggressive.

Voat is a platform for free speech, and thats good. People should say what they feel. And they should not be censored if their comments do not harm. I am not asking for mods and admins to limit the reddit related posts, even though I feel there are too many. Instead I want to get the community talking about their comments, about taking a deep breath before posting, rephrasing in a less aggressive manner. If Voat is to grow, then the community will begin to become like reddit. People feel lost in the crowd, they feel safe, like they are unaccountable. And they should, but thats no call for toxicity.

Look, its the Internet, I get that. I really do. This isnt going to be some Victorian gentlemen's club, all prim and proper. Conversation can get heated. Sometimes it needs to. But we are still small enough to talk about forming a core of polite users, who will engage with points of view different to theirs and listen. And if they still disagree, politely say "I'm sorry, I dont see any why we can agree. I do see your point of view on this point and that one, though I dont support them. Please consider this and that." It takes effort, sometimes it takes a physical shrug and deep breath. Sometimes it requires you to seem like you have lost, and just not reply.

Its also about not starting things. Want to make a point? See if there is a way you can make it without being inflammatory. If you have a controversial point, back it up with a source. If someone replies with an aggressive counter point, ask them to explain what they mean. If they reply with a troll comment, downvote and dont reply again, just move on (obviously many people cant downvote, but just move on from it then).

Look, I like the small community, I like how generally polite people are. I do still use reddit, for quick answers or larger discussions, things where the large community is a boon, and I plan to keep using it for as long as it fulfils that requirement. But Voat's draw is its sense of belonging to something. The recent toxicity towards reddit (and it is already spilling into political posts) could ruin that. At which point, with all due respect, Voat just becomes a smaller reddit with the seeds of all the same problems.

What do you think? How can we tackle trolls, build community spirit, without resorting to banning, censoring, etc? Perhaps an "anti-gold"? A user determined thing (a user being reported 20 times within a certain time?) that marks them with a black mark, and limits their posts and comments per day for a month? Or is that too subject to exploitation? Perhaps opening up downvotes to people at an earlier stage? But people have always had a tendency to downvote unpopular opinions regardless of how civil the comment was, so thats not flawless.

Or just trying to get the community to be, well, nicer to eachother? What are your thoughts?
